newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies Matria Healthcare injunction.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies Matria Healthcare injunction.

text.p: Matria Healthcare Inc said Thursday that a California superior court judge denied its request for a preliminary injunction to stop Adeza Biomedical Corp from terminating an exclusive marketing agreement for a pre-natal obstetric test.

In a statement, Matria executive vice president, Frank Powers said, "Although we are disappointed at the court's refusal to enjoin Adeza Biomedical from violating Matria's exclusive marketing rights, we expect a different outcome at the actual trial."
In a separate statement, Adeza, the maker of the test, quoted the court saying, "Matria has failed to satisfy its burden of showing that it is likely to succeed on the merits at trial."
Adeza said the court felt that it offered substantial evidence that Matria did not act in good faith in performing under the (exclusive) agreement.
Matria said it expects Adeza to continue to honor its obligation to provide it with the product under the exclusive marketing agreement.

Katherine Livingston, a lawyer representing Adeza said, "As far as we're concerned, we continue to supply Matria with the test, but on a non-exclusive basis, just like any other customer. We terminated the exclusive agreement in March."
The fFN test is the only U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved test for measuring fetal fibronectin, a protein that is a component of the placental membrane, Adeza said.

Adeza explained that fetal fibronectin has been demonstrated to be a biomedical marker predictive of pre-term delivery when found in the cervicalvaginal secretions of women with between 24 and 34 completed weeks of pregnancy.
"The evidence indicates that Adeza is likely to succeed in showing that within Matria there is an overall hostility towards sales of fFN", Adeza said, quoting the court.
In requesting the injunction, Matria, an obstetrical homecare and maternity management service said that it wanted to stop Adeza from marketing the test in competition with Matria.
